formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: The signer (owner) lets `spender` spend up to `value` axlUSDC from their balance. The allowance replaces any earlier one (ERC20Permit.permit calls _approve(issuer, spender, value)).
If value is type(uint256).max, the allowance never goes down when the spender uses it (ERC20.transferFrom skips the decrement).
The signature works only until `deadline` (block.timestamp > deadline reverts), and only once: it uses up the signer's current nonce.
formats.shown: The intent "Authorize spending of tokens", then the spender address (raw), the max amount in axlUSDC ("Unlimited" at or above 2^255), the expiry date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit has no test case, so no rendering of the amount, threshold or date is checked.
findings.evidence: FORMATS.md: 'cases: 0 (no tx)' for Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline). The code treats type(uint256).max as an allowance that never goes down: ERC20.transferFrom 'if (_allowance != type(uint256).max)'.
findings.fix: Add EIP-712 test cases: one with a finite value, and one with value = type(uint256).max to check that it shows "Unlimited".

findings.title: Permit intent does not name the spender or the amount; a sentence could carry both.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens", "interpolatedIntent" absent. The fields 'Spender' and 'Max spending amount' show both values.
